helpPanel.title: Activities guide
helpPanel.intro: Activities let a facilitator run structured, scored tasks inside a chatroom — quizzes, creative prompts, or research probes. This page covers the whole feature.

types.title: 1. Activity types
types.body: An activity type is a reusable template: a key, a name, the fields participants submit, and how each submission is scored. Create one here, then a facilitator starts it in any room the type's project can see.

schema.title: 2. Designing the submission form
schema.body: The Submission fields section defines what a participant fills in. Use the builder to add simple text/number/integer/yes-no fields, or switch to raw JSON Schema for nested objects, arrays, or enums the builder can't express.

validators.title: 3. Choosing a validator
validators.body: Every submission is scored server-side — never by the client. Built-in runs a scorer that ships with the platform and returns a verdict instantly. Webhook sends the submission to your own URL (through the egress proxy) and waits for a JSON verdict. MCP tool runs an MCP tool hosted on one of the project's agents. Webhook and MCP score asynchronously, so a submission is 'pending' until the verdict arrives.

activation.title: 4. Starting and ending an activity
activation.body: Only the room's creator (the facilitator) can start or end an activity type in that room. Participants can only submit while it is active; the platform enforces this server-side even if the UI is bypassed.

plugins.title: 5. Customizing the submission UI
plugins.body: Without a registered plugin, the room shows a form generated automatically from the submission fields — this covers most activity types with no extra work. A developer can register a fully custom plugin (e.g. a drawing canvas) for a type's key; the plugin only ever submits through a fixed host bridge, so it can't fake a score.

visibility.title: 6. Who can see a submission's content
visibility.body: Two switches on each activity type control this, but they are not fully independent. Agent visibility decides whether agents in the room (as context, not as a visible chat message) can read a summary of what was submitted — this is the master switch. Participant visibility decides whether the room's chat log also shows the content to other human participants, but only takes effect when agent visibility is on: a chat message visible to participants is necessarily visible to every agent reading that same room, so it can only add participants to what agents already see, never hide content from agents while showing it to people. Both default sensibly — agents on, other participants off.

retention.title: 7. Data retention
retention.body: By default, submissions are removed on the same schedule as the room they belong to. Setting a retention period on the activity type keeps its submissions for that many days instead, independent of the room's own lifecycle — useful when the activity is part of a research study.
